# Results — Study 754 (Beige-Book-Tone)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The Fed-watching folklore —
**a positive-tone Beige Book precedes an equity drift up** — tested as an event study on the
real Beige-Book release calendar (2011–2024, eight books/year) aligned to daily **SPY**
(yfinance, total-return adjusted). Tone is a **labelled Loughran-McDonald net-tone proxy**
(a small hardcoded, narrative-anchored reconstruction — **not** a live full-text dictionary
count; the scrape is the beat-7 extension), never presented under a real-tape banner. We
split per-event forward 1/3/5/10-day SPY returns by tone sign, add a Welch *t*, a placebo
null, a Newey-West (HAC) tone→drift regression, an ex-2020 regime test and a costed event
overlay. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Release tape | Beige-Book calendar (real Wednesdays) — **112 releases**, 2011-01-19 → 2024-12-04 (**79** positive-tone) |
| Tone | **Labelled LM-net-tone proxy** (z-scaled reconstruction; **not** a live full-text count) |
| Equity tape | yfinance daily **SPY** adjusted close (total-return adjusted), **3,586 rows**, 2010-10-01 → 2024-12-31 |
| Signal / entry | POSITIVE when tone > 0; enter at the **release-day close** (public by then — no look-ahead); hold *H* ∈ {1,3,5,10} trading days |
| As-of | **2024-12-31** · SPY fingerprint `eee0fc4ac90e` · releases fingerprint `dd4d39f56f19` |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The tone is a hardcoded, clearly-labelled
> reconstruction of the Loughran-McDonald net optimism of each Beige Book — public in spirit
> and anchored to each period's tenor (sunny 2013–2019, catastrophic spring-2020, gloomy
> 2022), but **not** a live dictionary count of the archived full text. Because the proxy is
> our construction we cannot *certify* magnitude either way; the verdict rests on the **regime
> confound** (which the proxy cannot manufacture away) and a synthetic control, not on the
> proxy's exact values. A full-text scrape is the beat-7 re-test.

## The signal — forward SPY returns after a POSITIVE-tone book vs the base rate

Entry at the release-day close; the base column is *all* releases. The believers say a
positive book should *raise* the forward return; Welch *t* compares the positive-set mean to
the unconditional mean (a real drift ⇒ **significantly positive** *t*). The placebo *p* is the
share of 20,000 random same-size event draws whose mean forward return is **at least** the
positive set's (i.e. as bullish or more).

| horizon | n positive | positive mean | negative mean | base mean | positive up-rate | base up-rate | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 79 | **+0.05%** | −0.40% | −0.08% | 51% | 48% | **+1.13** | 0.097 |
| 3-day  | 79 | **+0.24%** | −0.55% | +0.01% | 61% | 59% | **+0.95** | 0.169 |
| 5-day  | 79 | **+0.40%** | −0.83% | +0.04% | 68% | 64% | **+1.16** | 0.089 |
| 10-day | 79 | **+0.80%** | −1.15% | +0.23% | 67% | 61% | **+1.44** | 0.058 |

Read it carefully. The **direction matches the folklore** at every horizon: after a positive
book, forward SPY returns are **higher** than the base rate (e.g. **+0.40% vs +0.04%** at 5
days) and the up-rate is higher (**68% vs 64%**). But the gap is a few hundredths of a percent
and **never clears the significance bar** — the best Welch *t* is **+1.44** (10-day), placebo
*p* **0.06**. A right-sign tilt living well inside the noise.

## The dose-response — does *more* tone buy *more* drift?

OLS $r_H = a + b\,\text{tone} + \varepsilon$; the HAC *t* is Newey-West (Bartlett, 4 lags) on
the slope $b$. Releases are ~monthly, so multi-day windows barely overlap and OLS/HAC agree.

| horizon | slope *b* (%/tone-unit) | OLS *t* | HAC *t* | corr(tone, drift) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +0.27 | +1.46 | **+2.03** | +0.14 |
| 3-day  | +0.06 | +0.14 | **+0.14** | +0.01 |
| 5-day  | +0.38 | +0.77 | +0.93 | +0.07 |
| 10-day | +0.72 | +1.05 | +1.30 | +0.10 |

The slope's HAC *t* grazes 2 at **only the 1-day** horizon and **collapses to +0.14 at 3
days**, never recovering. An isolated crossing among four horizons — the kind multiple looks
manufacture — **not** a dose-response. **H₂ rejected.**

## The decisive confound — regime, not lead

Positive tone isn't sprinkled randomly through time; it clusters in expansions, and the few
gloomy books (2020, 2022) landed during crashes — dragging the *base* rate down and inflating
the positive-minus-base gap. Remove the single dominant regime (2020) and it dissolves.

| sample | positive − base, 5-day | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| full (112 releases) | **+0.36pp** | +1.16 |
| **drop 2020** (COVID) | **+0.21pp** | **+0.69** |

And corr(tone, the **prior** 5-day SPY return) = **−0.24** — the tone tracks recent conditions,
it does not lead them. What looked like a signal was the **equity risk premium sampled on the
Beige-Book calendar**, not the anecdote forecasting the tape. **H₃ rejected.**

## Tradability — the "long the post-release window on a positive book" overlay

Long SPY for the 5 trading days after each positive book, 1 bp one-way (round-trip 2 bp),
else flat. Annualised by trade frequency; buy-and-hold is total-return SPY over the same span.

| book | per-event (5-day) | annualised | note |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| overlay, gross | **+0.40%** | — | 79 trades, ~5.7/yr |
| overlay, net @ 1 bp | **+0.38%** | **+2.2%/yr** | event Sharpe **0.21** |
| all-events base | +0.04% | — | — |
| buy-and-hold SPY | — | **+14.2%/yr** | in market 100% |

The per-event window is mildly positive, but firing ~5.7×/yr for 5 days the overlay is **out of
the market ~90% of the time**, so it annualises to **+2.2%/yr** against buy-hold's **+14.2%**.
Costs aren't the issue — there's almost no exposure to a barely-positive, insignificant edge.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic release calendar + SPY-like series with a *planted* link (a positive-tone book
at *t* lifts the 5-day post-release drift by `edge`×tone). The detector must recover a planted
edge and must **not** manufacture significance when the true edge is zero.

| planted edge | n positive | positive 5-day | base 5-day | Welch *t* | slope *b* | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.000** (no link) | 62 | +0.18% | +0.33% | **−0.45** | −0.31 | −1.43 |
| **0.004** (large link) | 62 | +1.82% | +0.52% | **+3.16** | +1.70 | **+7.84** |

With **no** planted link the test sits at Welch *t* = −0.45 (HAC −1.43) — no false positive; a
large planted link drives Welch *t* to **+3.16** (HAC **+7.84**). The machinery is unbiased — so
the real-proxy null (best *t* ~1.4) is exactly what an *absent-or-tiny* tone→drift edge looks
like through this keyhole.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The folklore's **direction is real** — a positive book precedes modestly
  higher, more-often-positive forward returns at every horizon — but the excess **fails the
  *t* ≥ 2 bar** (best Welch *t* = +1.44, placebo *p* = 0.06), the dose-response HAC *t* clears 2
  at only the 1-day horizon before collapsing, and it leans on the 2020 crash. Literature
  supports the Beige Book's *economic* content; this tape cannot certify an *equity* signal.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The event overlay returns **+2.2%/yr** net vs buy-hold **+14.2%/yr**,
  in cash ~90% of the time. Almost nothing to harvest — before microstructure even bites.
- **Anecdote leads the tape? — NOT SUPPORTED.** Drop 2020 and the positive-minus-base gap falls
  to **+0.21pp** (*t* = 0.69); corr(tone, *prior* return) = **−0.24**. The Beige Book
  **describes** a cycle the equity market already priced — it does not lead the price. The whole
  appeal — reading the Fed's mood *ahead* of the tape — is the part the data rejects.
